requirements.description: Teen Patti Practice is a stateful three-card poker played against the dealer. The player antes, sees three cards, then folds and forfeits the ante or makes a fixed Play wager equal to the ante. The dealer qualifies with a queen-high hand or better; if the dealer does not qualify the ante pays even money and the Play pushes, and if the dealer qualifies the best three-card hand wins both wagers even money with ties pushing. Teen Patti ranks a trail highest, then a pure sequence, a sequence, a colour, a pair, and a high card, so a sequence outranks a colour. A Bonus pays on the player's own trail, pure sequence, or sequence regardless of the dealer. Deal and decision are exactly-once and reload-safe on the shared ledger and player-scoped state store.
requirements.notes: Allocated for GitHub issue #150, a catalog-expansion poker variant (#73). The service reuses shared card primitives and the ledger with its own three-card evaluator where a sequence outranks a colour.

requirements.description: Teen Patti Practice preserves authenticated player ownership, private dealer cards until showdown, one caller-stable action identity per deal or decision, replay of the identical committed result without another wallet movement, conflict rejection for changed action content, and reload recovery from committed ledger proof. The additive v1 contract exposes only game-owned state, rounds, and decisions routes and retains the standard success and error envelopes. English and Russian public controls remain accessible, responsive, reduced-motion safe, and restorable at the canonical route.
requirements.notes: Allocated for GitHub issue #150. The governed Browser case exercises real authenticated routes through the public game controls and rejects page overflow or fixed-feedback occlusion at all standard viewports.

requirements.description: Teen Patti publishes its active round, settled history, action receipts, opening and play recovery markers, rollback, and terminal settlement state through provider-current callbacks that replace only game-owned fields. Competing processes preserve unrelated player-state siblings and fail closed before a stale action or cleanup can overwrite the winning result, while the frozen v1 routes and envelopes, private dealer cards, caller-stable action identities, settlement ordering, replay behavior, rules, and economics remain unchanged.
requirements.notes: Private optimistic baselines never enter provider bytes or the public state payload. Production multiworker activation stays blocked because wallet and game-state publication remain separate durable boundaries.
